Building & Construction segment CAGR accelerating post-2027 as EU national renovation plans advance

Canada is projected to reach USD 123 million in revenue in 2035 and grow at a 13.4% CAGR (2026–2035). Oil sands, cold-climate pipeline requirements, and energy-performance standards support demand for thin, high-performance insulation. The market's industrial orientation creates an opportunity for products that reduce heat loss without imposing substantial weight or space penalties.

Europe held an 18.1% revenue share in 2025 and is forecast to grow at a 15.8% CAGR (2026–2035). Europe's aerogels market combines a policy-led building-renovation opportunity with automotive, industrial, and advanced-manufacturing demand. The pace at which national renovation programs become funded projects will be a major determinant of regional material consumption.

Germany generated USD 44 million in revenue in 2025 and is expected to grow at a 15.9% CAGR (2026–2035). Its large industrial base, automotive manufacturing footprint, and legislated retrofit environment provide several demand channels. Suppliers must navigate long qualification cycles and highly exacting construction and industrial specifications.

France accounted for a 3.0% share in 2025 and is forecast to grow at a 15.7% CAGR (2026–2035). Industrial process insulation and energy-renovation demand create a diversified application base. The market is well positioned for suppliers that can align technical performance with practical installation requirements in regulated construction projects.

Rest of Europe is projected to hold an 8.4% share in 2035 and grow at a 17.6% CAGR (2026–2035). Demand across this grouping is supported by industrial insulation, growing EV investment, and renovation programs. Market development will vary considerably by national construction practices, climate conditions, and the maturity of local advanced-materials distribution.

South Korea held a 4.0% share in 2025 and is forecast to grow at a 15.8% CAGR (2026–2035). Automotive production, electronics manufacturing, and LNG and petrochemical infrastructure create multiple demand channels. Its role in advanced battery supply chains makes qualification for safety-critical thermal applications especially relevant.

India is projected to generate USD 198 million in revenue in 2035 and grow at a 22.1% CAGR (2026–2035). Industrial expansion, vehicle-manufacturing investment, and construction activity underpin the opportunity. Local production capability and a growing need for efficient thermal-management solutions could make the market increasingly important to suppliers seeking regional scale.

Rest of Asia Pacific is projected to hold a 5.4% share in 2035 and grow at a 27.6% CAGR (2026–2035). Emerging EV assembly, LNG investment, and industrial-processing projects support a high-growth opportunity from a comparatively smaller starting base. Supplier success will depend on local technical support and the ability to adapt product formats to varied project and installation conditions.

Latin America is projected to hold a 4.5% share in 2035 and grow at a 16.7% CAGR (2026–2035). The Latin America aerogels market remains centered on oil and gas insulation, but automotive investment and construction demand are broadening its addressable base. Infrastructure cycles and local project financing will strongly influence the timing of demand.

Brazil held a 2.1% share in 2025 and is forecast to grow at a 16.9% CAGR (2026–2035). Deepwater operations and associated flow-assurance requirements support aerogel use in high-value insulation applications. The market is primarily driven by operational performance needs rather than general-purpose building-material demand.

Rest of Latin America is projected to hold a 0.9% share in 2035 and grow at a 23.7% CAGR (2026–2035). LNG, petrochemical, and industrial-development projects are expected to underpin demand across this diverse grouping. Adoption is likely to remain project-led, requiring suppliers to pair technical performance with localized commercial support.

The UAE generated USD 13 million in revenue in 2025 and is forecast to grow at a 12.6% CAGR (2026–2035). Demand spans industrial facilities and premium construction projects, where thermal performance and space efficiency are valued. Growth is comparatively measured because the market already has an established industrial insulation base.

South Africa is projected to hold a 0.5% share in 2035 and grow at an 18.7% CAGR (2026–2035). Mining, chemical processing, and emerging building-efficiency requirements support the opportunity. Market development will depend on project investment and broader adoption of energy-performance standards.
